setup:
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE requests AS
SELECT i::INTEGER AS id,
 CASE WHEN i <= 95 THEN 'fast' ELSE 'slow' END AS region,
 CASE WHEN i <= 95 THEN 100.0 ELSE 1000.0 END::DOUBLE AS latency_ms
FROM range(1,101) t(i);

examples.title: Two regions have very different request counts
Neither average of regional percentiles is the overall p95
examples.sql:
WITH regional AS (
 SELECT count(*) AS n, quantile_disc(latency_ms, 0.95) AS p95
 FROM requests GROUP BY region
)
SELECT (SELECT avg(p95) FROM regional) AS mean_of_p95,
  (SELECT sum(n * p95) / sum(n) FROM regional) AS weighted_mean_of_p95,
  quantile_disc(latency_ms, 0.95) AS overall_p95
FROM requests;

challenge.title: Find the overall discrete p99
challenge.prompt: Return one column, p99_ms, containing the exact discrete 99th percentile across all requests.
challenge.hint: Compute the percentile over request observations. An average of regional p99 values answers a different question.
challenge.starter: WITH regional AS (SELECT region, quantile_disc(latency_ms, 0.99) AS p99 FROM requests GROUP BY region) SELECT avg(p99) AS p99_ms FROM regional;
challenge.solution: SELECT quantile_disc(latency_ms, 0.99) AS p99_ms FROM requests;
challenge.success: The 99th sorted observation is a slow-region request: 1,000 ms. The tail can change sharply even when most requests are fast.
